facts.text: An intervention is an action a collision system takes on the machine when the operator has not acted: reducing speed, stopping the machine, or preventing the machine from starting to move.
facts.quote: An intervention is what a collision system does to the machine itself when the operator has not acted: it reduces speed, stops the machine, or prevents it from starting to move.

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 allows exactly three kinds of intervention for earth-moving machinery: speed reduction, stopping, and motion inhibit, meaning refusal of a command to move from standstill.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-1 allows exactly three kinds for earth-moving machinery: speed reduction, stopping, and motion inhibit (refusing a command to move from standstill).

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 never allows automatic steering as a collision-system intervention for earth-moving machinery.
ISO/TS 21815-2 defines the digital messages a collision system sends to a machine to slow down, stop, or prevent motion.
facts.quote: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines the digital messages a collision system sends to the machine to "slow down, stop or prevent motion" [Chapter 8].

facts.text: South African law specifies a collision-system sequence of detection, warning, and, if the operator takes no action, slowing to a safe speed followed by applying the brakes.
facts.quote: South African law describes the same sequence: detect, warn, then if no operator action, slow to a safe speed, then apply the brakes [Chapter 2].

facts.text: In a warning-only collision system, an unnecessary detection causes annoyance and distraction.
facts.quote: With a warning-only system an unnecessary detection costs annoyance and distraction.

facts.text: When a collision system can intervene, a false or nuisance classification becomes a machine-motion command, turning the error into both a human-factors and vehicle-dynamics hazard.
facts.quote: Once the system can intervene, a false or nuisance classification becomes a machine-motion command, so the same error turns from a human-factors problem into a human-factors and vehicle-dynamics hazard [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Underground workers describe collision-system stops as "jarring and jolting."
facts.quote: Underground workers describe "jarring and jolting" stops

facts.text: Mine leaders preferred collision systems that slow the machine to a crawl before setting the brake.
facts.quote: mine leaders preferred systems that slow the machine to a crawl before setting the brake [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Intervention is the new element in the Collision Mitigation System (CMS) relative to the warning system.
facts.quote: Intervention is the new element in the CMS.

facts.text: Evidence established by the warning system stops at the first brake command because recorded history no longer shows what the machine would do after intervention.
facts.quote: Everything the warning system proved stops at the first brake command; after that the recorded past no longer tells you what the machine would do

facts.text: Validating machine behavior after a CMS brake command requires new evidence from closed-loop simulation, bench tests, and proving-ground tests.
facts.quote: new evidence from closed-loop simulation, bench tests and proving-ground tests is needed [Chapters 1, 7].
